def parse_amount(text):
    # reject empty
    if text is None or text.strip() == '':
        raise ValueError('empty')
    # strip spaces
    s = text.strip()
    # allow dot or comma as decimal separator
    # replace comma with dot if exactly one comma and no dot? simple: replace comma with dot if comma present and no dot? spec: accept decimal dot/comma.
    # We'll normalize: replace ',' with '.' if there is exactly one ',' and no '.'? Simpler: replace ',' with '.' and then parse.
    # But '12,50' -> '12.50', '12.50' -> '12.50'.
    # Avoid replacing ',' in other places like '1,000' (thousand separator) but spec says decimal dot/comma, so assume only one separator.
    # We'll just replace ',' with '.' and then parse.
    s = s.replace(',', '.')
    # reject negative numbers
    if s.startswith('-'):
        raise ValueError('negative')
    # parse; float will convert 'inf'/'-inf' to inf/-inf, also 'nan'.
    # After replacement, check for non-finite.
    val = float(s)
    if not (math.isfinite(val)):
        raise ValueError('non-finite')
    return val
